claims.text: The material is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
An intact protective oxide film is present on the alloy surface at ambient conditions.
A protective oxide film is present along phase interfaces at ambient conditions.
Mechanical wear disrupts and removes the passivating oxide layer.
Wear-induced oxide removal occurs preferentially along phase boundaries.
Oxide-film removal exposes fresh alloy material.
Freshly exposed alloy surfaces are more susceptible to rapid corrosion.
Heterogeneity at phase interfaces promotes galvanic coupling.
Galvanic coupling between phases enhances localized corrosion.
Combined wear and corrosion produce total degradation significantly greater than the additive degradation from isolated wear and isolated corrosion.
The combined condition produces significantly higher localized corrosion at phase boundaries.
Sufficiently aggressive wear intermittently removes the oxide film.
Elevated temperature promotes rapid oxidation kinetics.
Elevated temperature promotes rapid corrosion kinetics.
The proposed mechanism is not expected to dominate when conditions fundamentally alter the oxide chemistry or alloy microstructure.
The magnitude and spatial distribution of degradation may vary with local alloy composition and testing conditions.

contradictions.description: The conditions require isolated controls under identical environmental conditions, while the baseline defines wear-only testing as being without active corrosion. Thus the wear-only environment cannot be fully identical to the combined corrosive environment unless 'identical' is restricted to temperature and non-corrosive parameters.
